To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the statistical downscaling techniques can successfully downscale the future precipitation, maximum and minimum temperatures at finer scale and the SDSM can be used for further hydrological modeling.
SDSM and LARS-WG are comparable in downscaling future climate variables of UBNRB.
SDSM using canesm2 GCM was the best model in simulating the future climate change for the UBNR.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the down scaling and projection of future climate scenarios for the UBNR basin using statistical down scaling models.
the application of two widely used down scaling techniques for the UBNR basin.

the development and application of a multi model statistical down scaling techniques for future climate scenarios in order to provide more reliable and useful information for the water resources and environmental managers in the UBNRB and beyond.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
both down scaling technique have their own advantages in terms of their performance and the choice of down scaling method depends upon the purpose of the application.
the SDSM model was able to reproduce the current local climate conditions better than LARS-WG.
both downscaling techniques are able to reproduce the current climate conditions of UBNRB with a good accuracy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
SDSM using canE SM2 GCM is the best performing down scaling technique for the study area.
both down scaling models are suitable for climate down scaling and the selection of down scaling model is dependent on the study objectives.

SDSM using canesm2 GCM is more suitable to downscale future climate change scenario of precipitation for hydrological modeling in the UBNRB, while LARS-WG using canESM1 GCM is more appropriate to simulate the future climate change scenario for Tmax and Tmin.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the SDSM using canesM2 CMIP-5 GCM is able to reproduce the current climate of UBNRB with high level of accuracy and can be used for future projection.

, the future precipitation will increase in most part of the basin with a slight increase of 1.2% in the whole basin, while the future maximum and minimum temperature will increase with a rate of 0.9% and 2.3%, respectively.

the downscaling techniques (LARSWG and SDSM) can be used as complementary methods for downscaling climate variables at local scale and the results are useful to support water resources management in the region.
